title: Victoria Street North redevelopment approved after deferral
subtitle: Affordable housing commitment, Grand River Rocks lease concerns, Ontario Land Tribunal risk and related planning by-laws
overview: Council approved an Official Plan amendment and a zoning change for 236-264 Victoria Street North, sought by Vicner Inc. The application had been deferred a week earlier so the applicant could talk with the existing tenant, climbing gym Grand River Rocks, about its lease {{vote:m1}}.

The Official Plan amendment goes to the Region of Waterloo for approval. Council also adopted the Urban Design Report, which staff will apply through site plan approval. The applicant's representative said written commitments had been sent to the City, including 32 affordable housing units. The applicant also made commitments about the tenant's lease. The tenant has asked for some lease amendments, and the owner had not yet reviewed them.

Many councillors said they wished the gym could be better protected. Staff advised that lease arrangements and these commitments fall outside what the Planning Act and the Ontario Land Tribunal consider, so they could be lost on appeal. The related by-laws were added as late items and passed the same day, completing the approval locally.
Residents should expect phased construction. The applicant said the part of the site nearest St. Ledger Street, where the gym is, would likely be built last.

decisions.item: Official Plan Amendment, 236-264 Victoria St N
decisions.detail: Council adopted Official Plan Amendment OPA24/001/V/CD for Vicner Inc. and forwarded it to the Region of Waterloo for approval {{vote:m1}}.

decisions.item: Zoning By-law Amendment, 236-264 Victoria St N
decisions.detail: Council approved Zoning By-law Amendment ZBA24/001/V/CD for Vicner Inc. in the form attached to Report DSD-2024-132.
Council adopted the December 2023 Urban Design Report and directed staff to apply it through the Site Plan Approval process.
Council gave third reading to the by-laws adopting Official Plan Amendment No. 51 and amending the Zoning By-law for the Victoria Street North site, which were added to the agenda as late items.

debate: Supporters said the application met Planning Act and Official Plan tests and had staff support. They argued that a refusal would likely be appealed to the Ontario Land Tribunal, where the affordable units and tenant concessions could be lost.

Several councillors welcomed the 32 affordable units, which the applicant was not required to provide. They also welcomed the commitment to keep the gym's lease for its remaining roughly four years. Others said this gave the tenant some certainty, though not the long-term assurance the gym's community wanted.

One councillor noted that an appeal would mean hiring lawyers and planners, at significant cost to the City. Another said lease terms are outside what Council can legally consider in a planning decision.

Opponents and undecided members stressed the gym's value, citing a large membership. They said displacing businesses matters as much as displacing residents. One noted the properties were rezoned fewer than five years ago and the zoning should be respected. Some said they were still not satisfied and could not support the application.

Questions of the applicant's representative covered the meaning of affordable (the representative pointed to CMHC criteria), the applicant's past development experience, and phasing. Council also heard that the City met its 2023 housing numbers but must keep issuing permits to reach the provincial pledge.
